items.t: COP31 deadlock persists as countries launch new ‘climate reality check’
items.d: With the clock running down at COP31 in Antalya, countries on Wednesday launched a new global check on whether climate promises are being kept, even as ministers remained deadlocked over some of the summit’s toughest questions: who pays, how fast the world moves away from fossil fuels and whether a greener future can be called “just” if poorer countries cannot afford it.

items.t: Patients running out of options as antibiotics stop working against common infections
items.d: Common bacteria are becoming highly resistant to front-line and even “last-resort” antibiotics, the UN World Health Organization (WHO) said on Wednesday, warning that the situation today is worse than it was in 2019.

items.t: Dozens more children killed in Yemen amid escalating hostilities
items.d: The UN child rights agency, UNICEF, on Wednesday called for warring parties in Yemen to protect children as renewed conflict between Houthi rebels and Government forces approaches the three-month mark.

items.t: Europe plans to catch the next computer chip wave
items.d: Europe hopes to be a leader in a new generation of computer chips which use light to process data.

items.t: As Trump and Xi meet, China's AI dreams face an unexpected hurdle: the Nvidia spy scandal
items.d: China worries the scandal could ramp up pressure on the US to further restrict the sale of advanced chips.
